headline: Day-Use Passes and Campground Booking for Golden Ears
reservation: A Day-Use Pass is often required for vehicle entry during peak seasons and must be reserved online through BC Parks, typically starting the morning before your visit. Camping must be booked through the separate provincial reservation system. Check the official site for the specific date range when the pass system is active.

days.title: Alouette Lake Recreation

stops.name: Alouette Lake South Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the expansive mountain views from the shore of this large, glacier-fed reservoir.

stops.name: Spirea Nature Trail
stops.detail: Walk through a moss-draped forest featuring interpretive signs about the local ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes from the park gate to the lakefront; conditions vary.
days.note: The beach area is the first to reach capacity; arrive early during summer months.

days.title: Waterfalls and Rainforests

stops.name: Lower Falls Trail
stops.detail: Follow the wide, flat path along Gold Creek to reach the cascading Lower Falls.

stops.name: Gold Creek Lookout
stops.detail: Observe the clear, emerald waters of the creek against the backdrop of the rugged peaks.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes from the main lake to Gold Creek parking; conditions vary.
days.note: Expect damp conditions on trails near the creek; boardwalks can be slippery.

days.title: Upper Elevations and Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from the West Canyon Trailhead

stops.name: West Canyon Lookout
stops.detail: Gain elevation for a perspective over the valley and the surrounding Coast Mountains.

stops.name: Viewpoint Beach
stops.detail: A rocky riverside spot perfect for a mid-hike break with views of the mountain peaks.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from Maple Ridge to the trailhead; conditions vary.
days.note: Higher elevation trails are significantly steeper and may have lingering snow in spring.

intel.title: Lot Capacity
intel.text: Parking at Gold Creek and South Beach is monitored by the Day-Use Pass system. Once designated lots are full, vehicles without a pass or reservation will be turned away at the park gate.

intel.title: Cellular Dead Zones
intel.text: Reception drops off rapidly once you pass the park gates. Do not rely on digital communication for emergencies; emergency phones are available at specific park locations.

intel.title: Last Services
intel.text: The final opportunity for fuel and major supplies is in Maple Ridge. There are no gas stations or grocery stores within the park's mountain boundaries.

intel.title: Gate Hours
intel.text: The park gates are locked nightly; check the official BC Parks page for current seasonal opening and closing times. Plan your return from deep trails accordingly to avoid being locked in.

intel.title: Road Conditions
intel.text: The main park road is paved, but access to certain trailheads may involve gravel sections. During heavy rain or snowmelt, monitor official alerts for potential road washouts or closures.

plan.arrival: Fly into Abbotsford (YXX) or Vancouver, rent a vehicle, and stop in Maple Ridge for bear-safe food storage containers and supplies before heading north.
plan.vehicle: Cars and small RVs are suitable for the main roads, but large RVs may find the Gold Creek parking area restrictive; check BC Parks for length limitations.
plan.goldenHour: Panorama Ridge offers a majestic view of the 'Golden Ears' peaks catching the light, though this requires a significant hike.
